summary: Oseltamivir is an oral influenza neuraminidase inhibitor active against influenza A and B. It is used to treat acute uncomplicated influenza (started within 48 hours of symptoms in patients 2 weeks and older) and for prophylaxis (patients 1 year and older). The prodrug is converted by hepatic esterases to the active oseltamivir carboxylate, which is renally eliminated and requires dose reduction in renal impairment. It is not a substitute for annual influenza vaccination.

moa: Oseltamivir phosphate is a prodrug hydrolyzed by hepatic esterases to the active metabolite oseltamivir carboxylate, an inhibitor of influenza A and B viral neuraminidase. Neuraminidase inhibition prevents release of newly formed virions from infected cells and limits viral spread within the respiratory tract.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to oseltamivir or any component of the product (including prior anaphylaxis or serious skin reaction)
relative: Severe renal impairment / ESRD not undergoing dialysis (not recommended)
monitor: Signs of abnormal behavior / neuropsychiatric events, especially in children

preg: Considered acceptable when indicated. Published observational data in more than 5,000 exposed women (including >1,000 first-trimester exposures) do not show an increased rate of congenital malformations. Pregnant women are at higher risk of severe influenza complications, which may favor treatment.
lact: Compatible with breastfeeding. Oseltamivir and its active carboxylate are present in human milk at low levels considered unlikely to cause infant toxicity; no serious adverse effects reported in breastfed infants.
renal: Active metabolite (oseltamivir carboxylate) exposure rises as renal function declines. Reduce dose for CrCl >30-60 mL/min (treatment 30 mg twice daily) and CrCl >10-30 mL/min (treatment 30 mg once daily). Adjusted regimens apply for ESRD on hemodialysis or CAPD. Not recommended in ESRD patients not undergoing dialysis.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment required for mild to moderate hepatic impairment; pharmacokinetics in severe hepatic impairment have not been established.

moderate: Live attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV, intranasal) - avoid LAIV within 2 weeks before or 48 hours after oseltamivir unless medically indicated, due to potential reduced vaccine efficacy
interactions.food: No clinically significant food interaction; may take with or without food (food may improve tolerability)
interactions.diagnostics: No specific diagnostic interference reported. Neither oseltamivir nor its carboxylate is a CYP450 substrate or inhibitor; no dose adjustment needed with amoxicillin, acetaminophen, aspirin, cimetidine, antacids, amantadine, rimantadine, or warfarin

missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered, except if it is near (within 2 hours of) the next scheduled dose; then skip it and resume the usual schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Reports of overdose are largely without adverse reactions; when present, effects (chiefly nausea and vomiting) resemble those seen at therapeutic doses. Management is supportive; there is no specific antidote.
